extracted.intended_audience: DoD/military contracting officers, A-76 study teams, acquisition managers and program staff involved in competitive sourcing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and lessons learned for planning, conducting, and defending OMB A-76 competitive sourcing studies in DoD installations, including preparation of the PWS, acquisition strategy, staffing, cost comparisons, and risk management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow announced ground rules for cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency decisions to perform services in-house are reviewed to ascertain whether the agency followed the announced 'ground rules' for the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Comptroller General will examine whether the agency applied the solicitation's rules consistently (e.g., both parties receiving identical PWS). Unreasonable bidder interpretations of the PWS are not grounds to set aside an award if the agency followed its announced rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation clarity and sufficiency to enable intelligent competition
rubrics_metrics.description: A procuring agency must provide prospective bidders with information sufficient to enable bidders to compete intelligently and on a relatively equal basis; an IFB need not eliminate all performance uncertainties and risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre-bid conferences, timely amendments, and visual inspections to clarify ambiguous specifications. Expect inherent contract risk; bidders must account for it in bids. Failure to sufficiently define specifications can lead to protests alleging inability to compete intelligently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent inclusion of contract administration and comparable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons must treat comparable administrative and overhead costs consistently between contractor bids and the Government (MEO) estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure agency adds contract administration costs (and other overheads) equivalently to both contractor bids and the Government cost estimate to avoid unfair advantage complaints. GAO focuses on whether agency calculations were consistent with solicitation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost capture and accounting methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands must capture and record costs accurately for the cost comparison; OMB A-76 provides guidance but leaves the cost-capturing method to the command or Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop or adopt a uniform cost accounting method/system (e.g., Activity Based Costing) to capture direct, indirect, G&A, and non-standard costs (volunteers, prison labor). Lack of standard methods causes delays and unreliable comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level playing field / best value consideration in A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 comparisons often center on comparing the lowest qualified bidder against the MEO, driving decisions toward lowest cost rather than holistic 'best value'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While A-76 allows modified best-value approaches, the process often culminates in selecting the lowest-cost offer after MEO adjustments. Consider whether and how to incorporate non-cost factors (e.g., past performance) without undermining fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and measurement of past performance in source selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular lacks guidance on how past performance should be measured for Government operations (MEO) or how it figures into the prescribed cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If past performance is used, set grading criteria and normalize scores for bidders lacking past performance data. Recognize MEO will often lack measurable past-performance data; evaluate whether past performance will add meaningful value to the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of inherently governmental functions vs commercial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish inherently Governmental functions from commercial activities; some functions are clear while many fall into a 'gray area'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to OFPP determinations and legal restrictions (e.g., fire and police services, some depot-level maintenance). Services may differ in categorization (e.g., ADP management). Maintain and document rationale for inclusion/exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify common families of services suitable for competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize service categories frequently opened for competition across Services to leverage commonality and potential consolidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common categories include Base Operating Support, Family Housing Management, Base Communications, Utilities/Heating, Library Services, Base Supply, Grounds Maintenance. Even common services can prompt protests; follow FAR and announced acquisition strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong management structure and senior leadership involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive sourcing studies require a sound management structure and senior management (installation commander) involvement to lend credibility and guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider forming an A-76 Council or Integrated Product Team (IPT), or a quasi program office for major studies. Centralized management mitigates stakeholder conflicts and helps meet timelines and budget expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing: full-time dedicated A-76 study team and program manager
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a full-time program manager and consider full-time study team members to meet schedules and maintain focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full-time staff improve schedule adherence but risk losing technical currency; mitigate by maintaining close interaction with the activity under study. Avoid conflicting supervisory relationships that create multiple bosses and increase conflict-of-interest risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent and identify conflicts of interest early
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and evaluate potential organizational conflicts of interest early in the acquisition process, per FAR 9.504.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile a conflict-of-interest database listing undesirable personnel; contracting officer should ensure SSEB/SSAC assignments avoid conflicts. Use military legal counsel to scrub personnel lists. Failure to address conflicts can invalidate evaluations and force recompetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a comprehensive acquisition strategy early
rubrics_metrics.description: The acquisition strategy is the single most important document for an A-76 study and should set the decision framework from program outset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include choice of contract type, evaluation approach, management of risks, staffing, and past-performance considerations. Revisit strategy as more is learned; ensure it aligns with customer needs and risk tolerance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select contract type appropriate to requirements maturity and risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose contract type early based on known requirements, cost-analysis maturity, and acceptable risk levels; options include Firm Fixed-Price (FFP), Fixed-Price-Incentive-Firm (FPIF), Fixed-Price Award-Fee (FPAF), and cost reimbursement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FFP is appropriate where scope is well-defined; avoid for highly variable-cost services (e.g., food services). Consider FPIF or award-fee to incent performance, and cost-reimbursement when work uncertainty is high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use award-fee contracts only when FAR conditions are met
rubrics_metrics.description: Award-fee contracts can motivate excellence but must meet FAR conditions before use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAR conditions include: administrative costs of award evaluations are justified by benefits; procedures for award evaluation are established; periodic evaluations are provided; award amounts are sufficient to motivate excellence; government's fee determination is unilateral and not subject to disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect proprietary information and avoid unfair leveling in MEO discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: During discussions with the MEO, contracting officers risk revealing proprietary information that could level the playing field in favor of the MEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct MEO discussions cautiously to avoid inadvertent disclosure. Avoid 'technically' leveling the playing field for the MEO; allow only necessary and defensible adjustments to MEO and document rationale to reduce protest risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) accuracy and scope fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS is the most important product in an A-76 study; it must reflect the scope and amount of work currently performed and avoid adding work ('gold plating').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inflating the PWS opens the command to protests and undermines projected savings (contractors bid on inflated PWS while MEO is built around current work). Contracting officer should advise IPTs from project inception and participate throughout PWS development.

rubrics_metrics.name: PWS development techniques and verification (WBS and ABC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use structured methods to develop and verify the PWS, such as a modified Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) and Activity Based Costing (ABC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break commercial activities into sub-components, validate requirements as you rebuild to major components, and have technical experts familiar with Government operations verify the PWS. ABC aids validation and cost capture where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing and composition of Source Selection teams (SSEB/SSAC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff the Source Selection Evaluation Board and Source Selection Advisory Council so assignments do not impose conflicts of interest or legal violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting officer input is critical. Ensure evaluators are beyond reproach, segregate evaluators from MEO developers, and prevent evaluators from accessing contractor proposal details improperly; improper staffing can require restarting the acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk identification and management (employee reaction, PWS, gold-plating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and manage risks such as employee reaction to outsourcing, PWS deficiencies, and 'gold-plating' requirements which can cause protests and cost escalation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat PWS development as the primary risk area and develop explicit mitigation steps (e.g., validation methods, stakeholder communications). Consider establishing risk registers and mitigation plans similar to major system programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider contract bundling and small-business impact (FAR 19.201)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware that bundling/omnibus contracts, while enabling economies of scale, may exclude small or disadvantaged firms; Government policy (FAR 19.201) seeks maximum practicable opportunities for small businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether bundling will preclude participation by small/HUBZone businesses and comply with FAR guidance to provide practicable opportunities. Factor small-business policy into acquisition strategy design.
